record.original_question: A hypersurface immersion is of 2-type when it is of finite type with exactly two distinct Laplace eigenvalues in its spectral decomposition. Study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^(n+2); in particular, classify 2-type hypersurfaces of S^4 in E^5.

evidence.quote: In particular, if all of the eigenvalues lambda1, . . . , lambdak associated with the spectral decomposition are mutually different, then the immersion x (or the submanifold M) is said to be of k-type.
Problem 2. Study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^(n+2). In particular, classify 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere S^4 in E^5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E^m$ denote Euclidean $m$-space with its standard inner product and Laplace operator $\Delta$ (acting componentwise on vector-valued functions). For an isometric immersion $x: M^n \to E^m$ of a connected Riemannian manifold, the position vector admits a spectral decomposition
$$x = x_0 + \sum_{i \in I} x_i, \qquad \Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i,$$
where $x_0$ is a constant vector, the $x_i$ are non-constant smooth $E^m$-valued maps, and $\{\lambda_i\}_{i\in I}$ are mutually distinct real numbers. The immersion (or the submanifold $M$) is said to be of finite type if the index set $I$ is finite, and of $k$-type if $|I|=k$. In particular, $x$ is of $2$-type when its spectral decomposition has exactly two distinct nonzero Laplace eigenvalues.

Now let $S^{n+1}(r) \subset E^{n+2}$ denote a round hypersphere of radius $r > 0$. Consider isometric immersions $x: M^n \to S^{n+1}(r) \subset E^{n+2}$ which are of $2$-type when viewed as immersions into $E^{n+2}$.

(a) Classify all $2$-type hypersurfaces $M^n$ of a hypersphere $S^{n+1}(r)$ in $E^{n+2}$.

(b) In particular, classify all $2$-type hypersurfaces of the unit hypersphere $S^4 \subset E^5$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere is a long-standing problem of B.-Y. Chen, included in his lists of open problems on finite-type submanifolds and reiterated in surveys on Riemannian submanifolds. Many partial results exist (e.g., for hypersurfaces with constant mean curvature, with at most two distinct principal curvatures, and various low-dimensional or curvature-restricted cases), but a full classification of 2-type hypersurfaces of $S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$, and even of $S^4\subset E^5$, remains open.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (B.-Y. Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing finite-type submanifolds and listing the classification of 2-type hypersurfaces in hyperspheres among unsolved problems, with several partial results.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere is listed as an open problem with only partial answers.
